title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1RC0RA_1LD0RB_0LE0LC_0LA0LC_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1RC0RA_1LD0RB_0LE0LC_0LA0LC_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the shift rules of the sweeps over the (10) sea and the only halting shape (1 1 E> 0). In 109 steps E read a 0 30,301 times, never with 1 1 to its left. The rounds follow a regular pattern, but the reshuffle at the end of a round is not worked out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 60,889 cells have been visited and 30,439 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.027). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.477).

claims.title: The sweeps' shift rules
claims.text: Rightward, A turns (01)^n into (10)^n, 2 steps a pair, and A or B with a 0 behind them cross the 0001/1000 markers; leftward, C crosses (01)^n and D crosses (10)^n unchanged, 2 steps a pair.

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: F on a 1 halts; F is entered only from A on a 1 (0LF), and A comes from B on a 1 (moving right, which leaves a 0 where F lands) or from E on a 0 (moving left). So it halts iff E reads a 0 with 1 1 to its left: 1 1 E> 0 reaches F on a 1 in 2 steps (the converse by reading the table, not formalized).

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In 109 steps E reads a 0 30,301 times; the three cells to its left (nearest first) are 101 30,093 times, 010 92, 100 50, 000 48, 001 18, never starting 11.

claims.title: Rounds
claims.text: Sampled with C on a 1 at the right end (once a sweep), the tape is 1 100 100 (10)^x0 1000 (10)^x1 100 (10)^x2 100 ... (10)^X 1000 (10)^Y plus a short end. During a round X drops by 2 and Y grows by 3 each sweep (from step 7.25·108 to 9.74·108: X 8477 → 2877, Y 18063 → 26463). When X runs out the small runs on the left change (e.g. 52,4,293,497,17 → 40,16,290,500,15 → 56,4,277,512,2) and a new round starts with a larger X: rounds began near steps 4.59·107, 1.01·108, 2.28·108, 5.11·108 with X = 5546, 8649, 12310, 18877.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs 1 1 E> 0, which the sweeps never produce; it would have to come from the reshuffle at the end of a round, whose rule (how the small runs change) has not been found.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 60,889 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Per sweep during a round; rounds about 2.2 times longer each.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: A (10) sea with markers
html: Almost all of the tape is 10 repeated. A few markers interrupt it: 100 or 1000. Written as runs (1x56 = 56 copies of 10, 1/2 = 100, 1/3 = 1000), the tape at step 974,444,280 (C on a 1 at the right end) is

sections.heading: A marker walking left
html: The head bounces across the whole tape (the shift rules over the 10 sea are proved in Lean). Each sweep moves the last 1000 marker two pairs to the left, and the run behind it gains three pairs: between steps 7.25·108 and 9.74·108 the last two runs went from 8477, 18063 to 2877, 26463. When the run in front of the marker is used up, the small runs on the left are rewritten and a new, longer round starts; rounds so far began near steps 4.6·107, 1.0·108, 2.3·108, 5.1·108.

sections.heading: No 1 1 behind E
html: F reading a 1 halts. Working backwards through the table, the only way there is E reading a 0 with 1 1 just to its left (Lean: halt_shape). In the sea of 10 two adjacent 1s never occur, and in 109 steps E read a 0 30,301 times without them. A halt would need the end-of-round reshuffle to produce 11, which has not been seen.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.027). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.477).
After 109 steps the tape spans 60,889 cells (180 left of the start, 47,016 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer over a tape of (10) runs separated by single 1000/100 markers: during a round one marker walks left two pairs a sweep while the last run grows by three; when the run in front of it is used up, the small runs on the left are reshuffled and a longer round starts.
family: bouncer with a moving marker in a (10) sea (rounds about 2.2 times longer each)
